reason: The loop-control rewrite is a small, distinct change on the timed n=512 path, with low correctness risk and no claim that it will help. The Strassen variant removes an output pass, but the measured three-buffer wrapper lost all ten pairs; this limited change may not address its larger costs. Vectorizing packing may help, though clang may already do so. The 32-row classical layout has a plausible working-set benefit but needs major pointer, tile, and store changes. One allocation has uncertain benefit and retains the rejected Strassen arithmetic. Transpose fusion rereads A sixteen times and adds substantial mapping and register risk. The single-product-buffer Strassen variant retains the measured wrapper's main costs. Tail splitting affects only the general fallback, not the fixed n=512 timing path, and adds boundary-access risk.
